**What I found**

The new invoice PDF formatter should be a new file inside the subsystem that already owns the billing export — `src/exports/invoice-pdf.js` — exposing one pure function that takes order totals and returns PDF bytes (the record calls this PLACE). The fact that decides it: `src/orders` publishes exactly one entry point, `src/orders/index.js`, and the existing caller `src/exports/billing-export.js:1` already goes through it; `src/orders/repository.js` is an internal module with no external caller.

So the planned import is wrong. Reading `src/orders/repository.js` from the formatter bypasses the orders entry point (cross-domain coupling) and skips `getOrderTotals`, which is where subtotal, tax, and total are derived (`src/orders/index.js:3-8`). The formatter should import nothing from orders at all: `runBillingExport` already has the totals and can pass them in.

**Why it matters**

Acting: one new file, one new export, zero new import edges into orders — the formatter stays testable with plain objects and the 21% tax rule keeps a single owner. Not acting: `repository.js` returns raw orders, so the formatter would re-derive tax, and the PDF and the export job could disagree on the same invoice. It also makes `repository.js` a de-facto public surface, which no rule currently forbids — this repo has no linter at all.

**Do this first**

1. Create `src/exports/invoice-pdf.js` exporting `renderInvoicePdf(orderTotals)` — no imports from `src/orders`.
2. Have `src/exports/billing-export.js` pass the `getOrderTotals(id)` result into it.
3. Ship the enforcement rule with it (gate E, `architecture-as-code-javascript`): `src/exports/**` may import `src/orders/index.js` only.

**What I did not check**

- Whether the formatter is worth building at all, and its internal design — gate M (`functionality-complexity-tradeoff`) and gate A (`architecture-guidelines`) did not run; `L` is a focused alias. Run `/alchemy M` and `/alchemy A` to close them.
- Which PDF library, and whether a PDF SDK belongs behind its own adapter — `/alchemy down` (`bring-down`).
- Runtime, co-change, shared-data, and failure pressure — out of Rapid scope; needs `/alchemy L` with an explicit full topology request.
- The enforcement rule itself is unwritten and unverifiable today: no `eslint`, no `eslint-plugin-boundaries`, no architecture config exists (`package.json` has no dependencies). `/alchemy E` closes it.
